territorial_scope.description: Federal statute whose operative Section 3 restricts State licensing of ADS-equipped vehicles.

evidence.quote: a State shall not issue a motor vehicle operator's license

summary.short: Would bar States from issuing motor vehicle operator's licenses for Level 4 or 5 ADS-equipped vehicles operated in a manner that discriminates on disability. Directs the Secretary of Transportation to seek a National Academies study on accessible ride-hail vehicle access.
summary.long: H.R. 4419, the Autonomous Vehicle Accessibility Act, was introduced in the House on 15 July 2025 and referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure. Section 3 provides that, in accordance with title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act, a State shall not issue a motor vehicle operator's license for the operation or use of an ADS-equipped vehicle at SAE Level 4 or Level 5 in a manner that discriminates on the basis of disability against a qualified individual with a disability. Section 2 defines disability by reference to 42 U.S.C. 12102, public transportation by reference to 49 U.S.C. 5302, a ride-hail ADS-equipped vehicle as an ADS-equipped vehicle offered for compensated pre-arranged transportation through an online platform and dispatched in driverless operation, and SAE terms by reference to SAE J3016. Section 4 directs the Secretary of Transportation to seek an agreement with the National Academies for a study on public transportation infrastructure changes and access options for ride-hail ADS-equipped vehicles. Section 5 authorizes $5,000,000 to carry out Section 4, available until expended. The text states no penalties, enforcement procedure or effective date.

relations.target_text: SAE International Recommended Practice J3016 (published April 2021, or a later revision adopted by the Secretary)
relations.note: SAE-defined terms (ADS-equipped vehicle, dispatch, Level 4, Level 5, driverless operation) take the meanings in J3016 as published April 2021 or a revision the Secretary subsequently adopts.

evidence.quote: SAE International Recommended Practice J3016, published in April 2021

notes: No enabling act, amendment, repeal or transposition is stated; the cross-references above are definitional or interpretive. Internal inconsistency: Sec. 2(3) defines 'ride-hail ADS-equipped vehicle', but the operative Sec. 3 prohibition refers to any ADS-equipped vehicle at Level 4 or 5, and Sec. 4 refers to ride-hail vehicles. 'Qualified individual with a disability' (Sec. 3) is not defined. Sec. 5 authorises $5,000,000 for the Sec. 4 study only. Text is the bill as introduced (15 July 2025), referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changes legal treatment in this bill. SAE levels 4 and 5 are categorical scope definitions in Sec. 2(5), not numeric thresholds. The $5,000,000 in Sec. 5 is an appropriation amount, not a threshold.
